articles.title: Liverpool vs Manchester United Red Card Decision Overturned
articles.summary: An independent regulatory commission has found that referee Sam Barrott made an error in sending off Manchester United defender Leny Yoro during Sunday's match.
articles.content: A crucial decision in Sunday's Liverpool vs Manchester United match has been deemed a clear mistake by an independent regulatory commission. The commission found that referee Sam Barrott made an "obvious error when sending off Manchester United defender Leny Yoro. The incident occurred early in the game at Anfield, with Yoro receiving a red card for bringing down Reds striker Alexander Isak as he sprinted towards goal. Debate has been ongoing about whether Isak's heavy touch would have allowed goalkeeper Senne Lammens to reach the ball before him. Referees' chief Howard Webb had initially stated that the decision was certainly not clearly wrong". However, Manchester United lodged an appeal with the Football Association for wrongful dismissal, and their one-match ban was subsequently removed on Tuesday. The independent commission has now published its written reasons, which reveal a unanimous verdict among its members. According to these documents, Yoro's foul would not have given Isak an obvious goalscoring opportunity. Key points highlighted in the commission's ruling include Isak's heavy touch on the ball and his subsequent loss of control, allowing the goalkeeper to intervene. In their view, Lammens would have been able to gather or smother the ball before Isak could shoot at goal. A review of the decision to send off Leny Yoro has led to questions about the referee's judgment during a recent match. The chief refereeing officer at Pro Ref, Webb, shared his thoughts on the incident in an interview for the Match Officials: Mic'd Up programme. According to him, there was some uncertainty over whether Isak would reach the ball before Lammens intervened. Webb explained that the referee's decision was based on a split-second assessment of the situation, and it seemed he believed Isak had a good chance of getting to the ball first. The VAR review aimed to determine if this decision was clearly incorrect, but ultimately concluded it wasn't. The independent panel reviewing the incident disagreed with the referee's decision, citing concerns over the validity of certain analysis presented by the club as evidence. The controversy surrounding the sending off of Leny Yoro by referee Barrott during the Liverpool vs Man Utd match has taken a new turn. According to reports, the Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel has backed Barrott's decision and the VAR John Brooks' decision not to recommend a review. This development comes as Manchester United Manager Mauricio Pochettino reacts to the sending off of Leny Yoro during the match against Liverpool. The five-person KMI Panel, which includes three former players and coaches, one Premier League representative, and one from Pro Ref, is due to publish its findings for the match week on December 2. The panel's backing of Barrott's decision has sparked further debate about the validity of certain analysis presented by Manchester United as evidence. Despite this, Pro Ref declined to comment on the story or the commission's findings, while Manchester United have been approached for comment but remain silent so far. Manchester United had submitted a video of a challenge by Brighton's Pascal Struijk on Wilson Isidor of Sunderland last month, which led to Struijk being shown a red card after a VAR review. However, an appeal by Brighton led to the suspension being removed, allowing Struijk to return to action and potentially paving the way for Yoro to face Brentford in the Premier League on Saturday. The Red Devils' frustration mounted as Polish referee Szymon Marciniak made several contentious decisions during the match. A potential opening goal for Manchester United was denied after Marciniak blew for what many observers considered a minor infringement by Youri Tielemans, allowing Amad Diallo's shot to be disallowed. The VAR system intervened once more to recommend a review of another incident involving Patrick Dorgu and Sporting goalkeeper Kaique Pereira. The Brazilian appeared to have inadvertently directed the ball into his own net before Dorgu's challenge, but the referee deemed it a foul nonetheless. articles.title: Dallas Cowboys Seek First Winning Streak of 2026 Season on Thanksgiving Day
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys are seeking their first winning streak of the 2026 season as they face off against the Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving Day.
articles.content: The Dallas Cowboys are seeking their first winning streak of the 2026 season as they face off against the Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving Day. The stakes are high for the Cowboys, who have struggled to find consistency this year. In contrast to their current struggles, the Cowboys were able to win three consecutive games under head coach Brian Schottenheimer in his first season in 2025. This impressive streak included victories over the Las Vegas Raiders, the Eagles, and the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving Day. The Cowboys' 51-30 victory over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday has given their owner and general manager, Jerry Jones, a glimmer of hope for the team's postseason prospects. Just days earlier, Jones had described his team as "a bad team following their loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Week 10. Jones' comments may have been harsh, but he seems more optimistic now that his team has finally tasted success. He believes that this victory will give them a much-needed boost and allow them to start building momentum towards the end of the season. Quarterback Dak Prescott is looking to continue his impressive form on Thanksgiving Day. If he replicates his performance against the Titans, which included 325 yards passing and four touchdowns, he will set a new record for most passing touchdowns on Thanksgiving Day in NFL history. Prescott's ability to excel under pressure is crucial as the Cowboys look to make a late-season push towards the playoffs. The Thanksgiving game against their division rivals, the Eagles, is a cherished event for Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott. He sees it as an opportunity to connect with fans and inspire young children who look up to him. For Prescott, putting on his uniform with the iconic John Madden seal is a privilege he doesn't take lightly. Every year, millions of kids watch the game and then rush outside to play their own version of football. Not everyone on the Cowboys team shares Prescott's enthusiasm for Thanksgiving, however. Defensive tackle Quinnen Williams has made it clear that he's not a fan of the holiday. According to Williams, the timing of Thanksgiving clashes with his strict training and diet regimen during the in-season period. He prefers to stay focused on his fitness goals rather than indulge in traditional holiday foods. Williams' stance on Thanksgiving is understandable given his commitment to staying lean and trim during the football season. While many people enjoy indulging in festive foods like macaroni, Williams has to resist the temptation this time of year. His discipline is likely to be tested as he takes to the field against the Eagles. The Cowboys will face a familiar foe on Thanksgiving, with starting quarterback Joe Milton leading the Eagles charge. Milton previously played for the Cowboys and was part of their practice squad before being signed by Philadelphia in October. The trade that brought Milton to the Cowboys from the New England Patriots dates back to April 2025. The Cowboys' recent surge in performance has been fueled by quarterback Dak Prescott's exceptional playmaking ability. His impressive numbers have earned him a spot among an elite group of NFL players who have achieved 300-plus passing yards and five-plus total touchdowns in consecutive games. This exclusive club now includes Prescott, Daunte Culpepper from the 2004 season, Tom Brady from 2007, and Ben Roethlisberger from 2014. With his outstanding performance over the past three weeks, Prescott has catapulted to second place in passing yards this season with a total of 3,049. Prescott's ability to play balanced football has been key to his success, allowing him to distribute the ball effectively among his teammates. The Cowboys' emphasis on running plays has paid off, with an average of 125.5 rushing yards per game since Week 10. This balance has opened up the playbook and made it easier for Prescott to exploit defensive weaknesses. Prescott credits the team's success to a combination of factors, including the physical play from the offense line in the run game and the ability of his receivers to get open. He believes that this balanced approach has allowed him to focus on making plays rather than worrying about individual responsibilities. The matchup between Lamb and Pickens of the Cowboys and Mitchell and DeJean of the Eagles will be a closely watched contest on Thursday. The Cowboys' wide receivers have been having a stellar season, with Lamb leading the NFL in receiving yards and Pickens ranking 11th. However, the uncertainty surrounding Mitchell's status due to his hamstring injury has added an extra layer of intrigue. Mitchell's availability for the game was questioned earlier this week when he didn't participate in the Eagles' walkthroughs on Monday. But after practicing fully on Wednesday, the team listed him without a game status on their final injury report, indicating that he will indeed play against the Cowboys. The Eagles' decision to list Mitchell as available has been confirmed by Philadelphia defensive coordinator Vic Fangio, who stated that his cornerback will be fine for Thanksgiving. This is good news for the Eagles, who can now focus on preparing for the game without any concerns about their top corner's availability. When the Eagles have possession of the ball, they plan to employ a ground-and-pound strategy with 2024 NFL Offensive Player of the Year running back Saquon Barkley leading the charge. Barkley has been in impressive form lately, recording a rushing touchdown in four consecutive games - his longest streak yet in his career. The Cowboys' run defense has struggled this season, allowing an average of 151.5 rushing yards per game, making them vulnerable to Barkley's aggressive running style. Both Schottenheimer and Williams have described Barkley as a jump cut" runner, capable of smoothly hitting the hole and then gliding to a different spot on the line of scrimmage. The key to stopping Barkley is to contain his feet before he gets going, according to Williams. He compared Barkley's style to that of Bucky Irving, who had success against the Cowboys in Week 5, averaging a career-high 7.9 yards per carry in their matchup at AT&T Stadium. The Eagles' defensive tackle, Jordan Williams, is a force to be reckoned with this season, having racked up an impressive 18 tackles for loss so far. This number puts him at the top of the NFL's defensive tackles in that category, and it's also the highest total by any defensive tackle since 2022. Williams' prowess doesn't stop there - he has also put pressure on opposing quarterbacks with a league-leading 40 quarterback pressures this season. Moreover, he shares the lead among defensive tackles for forced fumbles with his teammate Jalen Carter. The Cowboys defense, however, has been struggling to contain high-scoring opponents, having allowed 20 or more points in 18 consecutive games - a streak that is currently the longest active one in the league. That particular record has not been matched since the Jacksonville Jaguars' run of 25 straight games from 2019-2021. The Dallas Cowboys are seeking their first winning streak of 2026 as they prepare to face the Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving Day. A key factor in determining the outcome will be whether quarterback Gardner Minshew is able to play, as his presence would significantly bolster the Eagles' offense. Prescott's impressive home record against NFC East opponents has been a major contributor to the team's success this season. With 20 consecutive victories at home against divisional foes, he stands tied with Tom Brady for the longest such streak since the AFL-NFL merger. articles.title: Concacaf W Championship Begins This Week
articles.summary: The tournament serves as a crucial stepping stone for national teams in the region, with World Cup and Olympic berths up for grabs.
articles.content: The wait for high-stakes women's soccer action is over, and the 2026 Concacaf W Championship is here to keep fans on the edge of their seats. The tournament serves as a crucial stepping stone for national teams in the region, with World Cup and Olympic berths up for grabs. The competition will feature eight national teams from the Concacaf region, all vying for a spot in the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup in Brazil and the 2028 Summer Olympics. The knockout bracket is set to kick off on Friday, November 27, with the stakes higher than ever before. Fans can catch all the action live on CBS Sports Golazo Network and Paramount+, with every game airing at Eastern Time. The tournament schedule has been released, with the third-place match and final taking place on Saturday, December 5. The Concacaf W Championship is a prestigious event that doubles as the region's qualifier for both the World Cup and the Olympics. This year's edition introduces a new format, sending teams directly to the 2027 World Cup and 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. In a significant change from previous years, the top two ranked teams in the Concacaf W Championship have earned byes into the tournament. The United States and Canada will automatically advance to the quarterfinals, while the remaining six teams, Jamaica, Costa Rica, Mexico, Panama, Haiti, and El Salvador, secured their spots through the Concacaf W Qualifiers. The new format has raised the bar for all participating teams, with the winner of each match moving one step closer to securing a coveted spot in the World Cup or Olympics. The road to the championship is long and arduous, but one thing is certain: only the strongest will emerge victorious. The Concacaf W Championship has undergone significant changes this year, eliminating group stages in favor of a single quarterfinal that determines direct qualification to the 2027 World Cup. The winners of each quarterfinal will secure their spots in the World Cup, while losers will compete in a play-in round with the two winners advancing to the inter-confederation playoffs in February 2027. The stakes are high for teams vying for a spot in the Olympics as well, with the top three finishers earning qualification for the 2028 Summer Games. However, since the United States is hosting the Olympics and has automatic qualification, the fourth-place team will secure the remaining Olympic spot if the USWNT finishes outside of the top three. The US women's national team faces a new opponent in El Salvador, marking their first-ever meeting with the team. This encounter comes on the heels of their match against Zambia in the Olympic group stage last July, where they showcased their dominance and clinical finishing. The reigning champions have an impressive track record, having won the last three Concacaf W Championship tournaments and holding a record nine titles overall. Their recent performances are equally impressive, having won all five games without conceding a goal in the 2022 tournament and outscoring opponents by a margin of 13-0. Manager Emma Hayes has made some adjustments to her roster following the 2026 NWSL Championship, replacing Trinity Rodman with Jaedyn Shaw due to a shoulder injury. However, Shaw will not be part of the team as Lia Godfrey takes her place on the U-23 roster, solidifying the USWNT's lineup for the upcoming tournament. The USWNT's U-23 roster has undergone another change ahead of the upcoming tournament. Laney Rouse, a Kansas City Current defender, will not be part of the team due to an injury or illness that has forced her out. In other news from the Concacaf W Championship, El Salvador is set to make its debut in the Women's World Cup qualifying process. They secured their spot by winning Group F with three clean sheets against Honduras, Barbados, and Trinidad & Tobago. Head coach Eric Acuna will lead El Salvador into this new challenge despite previous controversies surrounding his conduct. The team is trying to move forward under the leadership of Brenda Ceren, who was the top scorer in the Concacaf W Qualifiers with five goals. articles.title: Rock carvings in Scandinavia may have served as signposts for hunting grounds
articles.summary: A new study suggests that ancient rock art in Scandinavia was used to mark areas where animals congregated or could be driven into rapids, challenging the conventional notion of rock art as solely an expression of human creativity and emotion.
articles.content: Rock carvings from the Early Stone Age in Scandinavia have been the subject of much debate regarding their purpose. For decades, experts have pondered whether these intricate images were merely decorative or served a more practical function. A new study published in World Archaeology has shed light on this mystery, suggesting that these rock carvings may have been used as signposts to mark hunting grounds. The researchers propose that the images indicated areas where animals would congregate at natural crossings or could be driven into treacherous rapids. The study's authors emphasize that these ancient artworks should not be viewed solely through an artistic lens, but rather considered as tools with a practical application in the surrounding landscape. This perspective challenges the conventional notion of rock art as solely an expression of human creativity and emotion. Rock art in Scandinavia began to appear around 9,000 B.C., typically depicting large animals such as elk and reindeer near water sources or on steep rock faces. Initially, these images were often life-size or larger, but over time they evolved to include smaller figures interacting with one another and, eventually, people. The study's findings suggest that the purpose of rock art in Scandinavia underwent a significant shift around 5,000 B.C., transitioning from primarily depicting animals to more narrative scenes featuring humans. The researchers behind the study took a closer look at the animals depicted in the older images, considering factors such as age, sex, and relationship to their surroundings. Four ancient rock art sites were examined - Stykket in Trøndelag and Landverk, Gärde, and Duved in Jämtland, Sweden and Norway. The locations of these sites are significant, as they feature natural crossings over fjords and rivers. At these sites, images of animals were found standing at the water's edge, possibly drinking or preparing to cross. Some even appear to be walking towards a powerful rapid that would make the water treacherous. The large images would have been easily visible from a distance, especially from across the water. This placement makes them effective markers for traveling humans who could spot them while navigating by canoe or on foot along riverbanks. At one of these sites, Landverk, two elk were found with lines carved mainly over their hearts and lungs. This may indicate that these images marked specific hunting grounds where animals could be easily killed in a single shot. The researchers had to physically visit the sites to reach their conclusions. Visiting these remote locations provided a unique perspective on the rock carvings that is difficult to replicate in an academic setting. Associate professor Tomas Persson of Lund University noted that even those familiar with the literature often underestimate the impact of viewing these images in their natural context. The experience can be quite different from what one might expect, almost as if you're stepping into an art museum instead of examining a rocky outcropping. The study's authors emphasize that multiple interpretations are possible for these ancient images. This includes the possibility that they were used for shamanic or animist purposes in addition to their potential as signposts. While the researchers' approach cannot prove this, it does not rule out the idea either. Some of the earliest Scandinavian rock carvings may have had a practical purpose beyond mere artistic expression. The study suggests that these images could have marked specific areas where hunting was more likely to be successful. This theory is based on an analysis of the imagery and its placement within the landscape. The question of why these early images became more narrative in nature remains unanswered. According to the authors, archaeology often yields complex and nuanced explanations for historical phenomena, and this case is no exception. Associate professor Michael Ranta of Linnaeus University notes that attempting to understand these enigmatic images can be a rewarding experience even if it does not provide complete clarity on the matter. The researchers acknowledge that their study is limited to just four sites, but they propose extending the signpost hypothesis to other areas. This extension could potentially provide a more comprehensive understanding of the enigmatic images found in Scandinavia's Early Stone Age rock carvings. By examining these images within the context of landscape and hunting practices, the researchers suggest that they may have served as markers for specific hunting grounds. Understanding the purpose behind these ancient carvings can be a fascinating and rewarding experience. Phys.org : https://phys.org/news/2026-11-early-stone-age-scandinavia-signposts.html

articles.content: Meghan Markle is gearing up for her first Thanksgiving celebration since moving back to Britain from California's Montecito area. The Duchess of Sussex has shared some insights into her festive hosting style in a forthcoming winter issue of Bon Appétit magazine. As she prepares to host family and friends, Meghan reveals that her approach to holiday entertaining remains unchanged despite her busy schedule. In the magazine, she talks about various aspects of her life, including her favorite restaurants, her Netflix series With Love, Meghan, and her personal experiences as a college student. Meghan's passion for cooking dates back to her university days when she watched Rachael Ray's 30 Minute Meals show regularly. She recalls making a sophisticated grilled cheese sandwich in her first apartment by layering fontina, apple slices, and thyme between two slices of bread, pressing it on a George Foreman grill, and finishing it with olive oil and Maldon sea salt. The wine pairing for this dish was Trader Joe's Two Buck Chuck, which Meghan humorously describes as "Early 2000s at its finest." Meghan Markle's approach to hosting a special gathering is all about subtle touches that elevate an ordinary occasion into something truly memorable. She believes that it's these little details that make all the difference when loved ones are present. To prepare for her guests' arrival, Meghan likes to set the table ahead of time, freeing herself up to focus on enjoying their company. This thoughtful approach allows her to be more present and engaged with those around her. By doing so, she creates a warm and welcoming atmosphere that makes everyone feel at ease. When it comes to providing for overnight guests, Meghan goes above and beyond. She programs the coffee machine to brew before they wake up, ensuring that they have a freshly made cup of coffee to start their day. In addition, she stocks the kitchen with an assortment of breakfast essentials, including bagels, berries, yogurt, smoked salmon, and capers. To make things even more convenient, Meghan leaves a handwritten note inviting her guests to help themselves. For those times when Meghan is not hosting but rather attending someone else's gathering, she prefers to bring something edible and homemade as a gift. Her go-to options include honey-roasted spiced nuts or a blackberry pound cake that can easily double as breakfast the following morning. Presentation also plays a significant role in Meghan's approach to entertaining. She recommends using simple yet thoughtful touches such as kitchen twine, a length of ribbon, or a sprig of rosemary to add a personal and considered feel to any dish or presentation. As Ever, Meghan Markle's lifestyle brand, has been focusing on gift-giving with a new holiday collection that showcases thoughtful and personalized presents. The launch of this collection was marked by a heartwarming video featuring Princess Lilibet helping her mother make raspberry jam earlier this fall, highlighting the joy of family involvement in cooking and baking during the holidays. This year's Thanksgiving celebration is a significant milestone for the Sussexes as they mark their first holiday on British soil since 2018 and their first UK Thanksgiving with both Archie and Lilibet. articles.title: Elasmobranchs Respond Differently to Sensory Deterrents in Fisheries
articles.summary: A recent study on elasmobranch species has highlighted the complexities of using sensory deterrents to prevent bycatch in fisheries, with varying results across different species.
articles.content: A recent study on elasmobranch species has highlighted the complexities of using sensory deterrents to prevent bycatch in fisheries. The research, conducted at Charles Darwin University, focused on a subset of fish that includes sharks and rays. The investigation aimed to determine whether these creatures respond differently to various forms of deterrents. Elasmobranchs are facing an alarming rate of extinction, with overfishing being a major contributor. According to conservation guidelines, nearly one-third of all elasmobranch species are threatened with extinction due to unsustainable fishing practices and bycatch. The study's findings have significant implications for fisheries management, particularly in the context of net gear, which poses a substantial threat to these marine animals. The effectiveness of sensory deterrents in preventing bycatch varied significantly between species. While green LED lights initially deterred giant shovelnose rays, their deterrent properties wore off over time. In contrast, brownbanded bamboo sharks remained undeterred by both the LED light and other devices. According to lead author Emily Taljaard, the study's findings highlight the need for tailored approaches to reducing bycatch. This involves testing solutions on species that are directly affected by fishing practices. As bottom-dwellers, giant shovelnose rays have unique sensory adaptations that may not be compatible with existing deterrent technologies. Taljaard emphasized that a one-size-fits-all approach is unlikely to succeed in preventing bycatch. Different species interact with their environment and respond to stimuli in distinct ways. By understanding these differences, researchers can develop targeted solutions that address the specific needs of each species. The study's next phase will involve testing deterrents on a broader range of commercially relevant species. Researchers also aim to explore alternative device settings and placement strategies to optimize bycatch reduction efforts. Northern Australia is grappling with the ongoing challenge of bycatch in fisheries management. The region already has robust controls in place to minimize interactions between threatened species like sawfish and fishing gear, but more needs to be done. Researchers are exploring innovative solutions to reduce bycatch, and one promising area of investigation involves sensory deterrents that aim to repel sharks and rays from fishing nets. These early trials are crucial for understanding what types of deterrents might work best in real-world applications, but more extensive testing will be necessary before any large-scale implementation can occur. articles.title: Millions of Americans use AI platform Remento to preserve loved ones' memories during Thanksgiving travel season
articles.summary: Families can now record and compile conversations with elderly relatives using an AI-powered platform called Remento.
articles.content: As millions of Americans prepare for Thanksgiving travel, families may see this holiday season as an opportunity to connect with aging loved ones and preserve their memories. For Charlie Greene, cofounder and CEO of Remento, a new AI startup, the importance of recording memories was driven home by his own experience losing his father in the 9/11 terrorist attack. His father's plane crashed in Shanksville, Pennsylvania, leaving behind only old home videos as reminders. Greene has since become fixated on preserving loved ones' memories after his mother, Claudette, was diagnosed with stage-three lung cancer. He sought to conduct an oral history interview with her using questions like "How did you get to elementary school as a kid?" which brought out a spark in her despite the morbid context. The experience left Greene reflecting that it didn't feel morbid at all, but rather a way to connect with his mother and learn more about her life. He noted how surprising it was that she lit up when asked about her childhood experiences. Greene's mother is now in remission, but the experience has stuck with him as he launched Remento in October 2023. The platform sends weekly reminders to older "storytellers to respond to photos or questions chosen by family members, such as What was the hardest thing you had to overcome as a child?". These prompts can be customized in advance to fit the needs and interests of each family, allowing them to tap into their loved ones' life stories and create lasting memories. The AI-powered platform allows users to input conversations with their elderly relatives, which are then converted into a cohesive narrative. This narrative is compiled into a physical book that includes images and QR codes linking the text to the original recordings, providing an immersive experience for family members. Greene emphasizes the significance of Thanksgiving in facilitating these conversations, as it offers a unique opportunity for people to discover new memories or gain fresh perspectives on familiar stories from their relatives. He shares his own desire to have his daughter sit with her grandmother and hear her recount fond memories, highlighting the importance of preserving family history through this platform. The company has secured significant funding, including a $300,000 investment from Mark Cuban last year in exchange for a 10% stake, bringing its total raised to $4.3 million since launch. The use of AI technology in Remento's platform has surprisingly received less criticism than expected, according to its founder. Investors are drawn to AI because it holds immense promise, but Greene believes people want solutions to their problems and they expect consumer tech to deliver. This mindset shift is also reflected in the growing demand for AI-powered tools that make storytelling easier. Kindred Tales, a rival platform, has noticed this trend among its customers. The company offers both an AI-enhanced version and a non-AI version of its product, with the former providing speech-to-text transcription and some basic editing capabilities. In fact, before 2025, only about half of Kindred Tales' customers opted for the AI-powered option, but after that year, this number surged to 80%. The AI-powered tool has enabled Kern to efficiently manage his workload, freeing up time to focus on other aspects of the business. He has leveraged the technology to automate tasks such as email filtering and content creation, previously outsourced to freelancers. Greene emphasizes that despite its limitations, the AI solution has had a profound impact on users' ability to capture cherished moments with their loved ones. This has resulted in a significant increase in customer satisfaction, with 80% opting for the AI-powered option by 2025. The company's mission of making human experiences more seamless and engaging has been fulfilled through the judicious application of AI technology. By empowering people to create lasting memories with family members, Remento is leaving a lasting legacy. articles.title: Central Asian Kok Boru Match Played Out on Sun-Drenched Field
articles.summary: A group of men engaged in a fierce game of kok boru, Kyrgyzstan's national sport, which involves wrestling over a headless goat carcass and trying to score goals by carrying it into a cauldron-like target.
articles.content: A group of men on horseback engaged in a fierce game of kok boru, Kyrgyzstan's national sport, which involves wrestling over a headless goat carcass and trying to score goals by carrying it into a cauldron-like target. The intense match was being played out on a sun-drenched field in Don-Aryk, with the riders using all their strength to wrench the goat from each other's grasp. When one of them finally managed to gain control, he charged towards the goal, dodging and weaving around his opponents. The crowd watched anxiously as the outcome hung in the balance. I was watching this spectacle two weeks into a journey across five Central Asian countries with a group of mostly retirees who had joined me on the Smithsonian Journeys trip. Initially, I thought our differing ages would be a barrier to forming connections, but I soon discovered that my fellow travelers were warm and welcoming. As we took a break from the heat and watched the kok boru match together, one of them turned to me with a mischievous grin and invited me to join in on a victory lap around the field - carrying the goat, no less. Penny's story of resilience in the face of tragedy was a stark contrast to my own family's struggles with depression and agoraphobia. Her ability to keep traveling even after surviving a terrorist bombing in Bali that claimed three lives from her group was a testament to her unyielding spirit. This experience had also taken a toll on her husband, who suffered brain damage and became withdrawn; yet Penny continued to explore the world, often alone. As we bonded over meals in Khiva's markets, I began to see that age was not a barrier to experiencing life to its fullest. As we traveled through Central Asia, a sense of camaraderie began to emerge among our group. Despite my initial reservations about joining a tour, I found myself forming strong bonds with my fellow travelers. They would often appear at just the right moment, offering a listening ear or a comforting presence when needed. One of them, Linda, stood out as an exceptional individual - an 80-year-old retired psychoanalyst who shared my wicked sense of humor and attention span during the dull stretches of museum tours. Her irreverent spirit was infectious, making even the most tedious experiences more bearable. The group's collective attitude towards life was a constant source of inspiration. Susan, another member, had faced numerous health challenges, including two comas and a stroke, yet she still exuded vitality and enthusiasm. Her bold fashion choices - like wearing fire-engine red lipstick at 83 - left an indelible mark on me. As I observed my fellow travelers, it became clear that they were not just accomplished individuals but also resilient ones. A pulmonologist here, an oncologist there, or a former head of an ICU department - their impressive backgrounds only added to the sense of awe and respect I felt towards them. As I sat on the bus, surrounded by a group of seniors embarking on a Viking river cruise, I noticed that they didn't hesitate to ask for medical assistance whenever needed. It seemed like half the passengers were familiar with doctors and could easily summon them if required. Conversations with these travelers often turned into lively discussions about history and architecture. Some even had impressive backgrounds in medicine, adding an extra layer of depth to our conversations. I couldn't help but think back to my own father, who was always eager to share his knowledge on various topics - a trait that I had grown up appreciating, only to realize how much I missed it later. The group's discussions often touched on the topic of family and their adult children's lives. Would they find the right partner? Start a family? Live up to their potential? These questions were laced with a deep sense of tenderness and concern for one another. It was clear that these seniors had experienced life's ups and downs, but still held onto hope for their loved ones. As I reflected on our interactions, I realized that traveling with seniors requires patience - not just because some may use canes or walkers, but also due to the deliberate pace of itineraries designed to accommodate them. However, this slower approach allowed us to truly connect and appreciate each other's company, making the experience all the more enjoyable. As we traveled together, our differences became less apparent and a sense of camaraderie grew among us. I found myself looking forward to joining group trips and being surrounded by people who were eager to share their experiences and wisdom. The dynamics within the group shifted from one of mentorship to mutual appreciation. In these moments, I began to appreciate the value of slowing down and connecting with others on a deeper level. Our interactions became more meaningful as we shared stories and laughed together, creating a sense of community that was both unexpected and welcome. It's a feeling that has stayed with me long after our trips have ended. This experience has given me a new outlook on growing older, one that is filled with possibility and joy. articles.title: Cairo Fuel Tanker Accident Leaves 31 Dead
articles.summary: At least 31 people have died in a catastrophic accident involving a fuel tanker that overturned and caught fire on a major highway surrounding Cairo.
articles.content: Egyptian authorities have taken into custody a driver suspected of causing a catastrophic accident that has left at least 31 people dead in Cairo. The incident occurred on Wednesday evening when a fuel tanker overturned on a major highway surrounding the city, sparking a massive fire that engulfed the area and trapped vehicles and pedestrians. The inferno raged for hours, forcing firefighters and rescue workers to battle the blaze and pull survivors from charred cars. Traffic on the Ring Road, which links Cairo to neighboring governorates of Giza and Qalubiya, was severely disrupted as the fire spread, but by daybreak Thursday, normalcy had largely been restored. The area is still scarred by the disaster, with soot and charred remains visible everywhere, according to an AP video. The driver's actions are being investigated by authorities, who have launched a probe into the cause of the accident. Firefighters and rescue teams worked tirelessly to put out the fire and extricate people from trapped vehicles, but not before several lives were lost in the inferno. One survivor, a microbus driver named Salah Ahmed, recounted his harrowing experience when he was caught up in the chaos on the highway. I was just waiting for my turn, he said, when suddenly I saw flames engulfing everything around me. The scene on the Ring Road was described by one witness as "God's hellfire". The aftermath of the fuel tanker crash is still causing shock among locals who are struggling to come to terms with the disaster. According to official figures, 27 vehicles were left charred and 26 people were injured in the fire. Authorities have confirmed that DNA investigations are underway to identify the victims of this tragic accident. The public prosecutor's office has announced that it has detained the driver suspected of causing the fuel tanker to overturn. In a statement posted on Facebook, prosecutors revealed that the driver claimed he was speeding between lanes when he collided with the oil tanker from behind. Commuters and pedestrians who stopped at the scene on Thursday were met with a stark reminder of the disaster's impact. Black scorch marks disfigured the metal railings of one highway exit, where hundreds of vehicles had been trapped just hours before. The driver's words echoed the frustration felt by many Egyptians, who are all too familiar with the dangers of their country's roads. Most of those killed in the tanker crash were likely on their way home from work or school, according to Ahmed. Families gathered outside nearby hospitals as they struggled to come to terms with the tragedy, while the injured continued to arrive at emergency facilities for hours after the fire had been extinguished. In a desperate bid to respond to the disaster, authorities dispatched 39 ambulances to the scene. The incident highlights Egypt's poor transportation safety record, which claims thousands of lives every year. Speeding, inadequate road infrastructure, and lax enforcement of traffic laws are all contributing factors in these deadly crashes. articles.title: San Antonio Spurs Fall to Trail Blazers in Late-Game Collapse
articles.summary: The San Antonio Spurs' defense imploded in the final seconds, allowing a three-pointer that secured a 116-111 win for the Portland Trail Blazers.
articles.content: The San Antonio Spurs' late-game defense imploded in Portland, allowing a crucial three-pointer to be made and securing a 116-111 win for the Trail Blazers in their NBA Cup matchup. The Spurs had been dominant for most of the game, but Deni Avdija's shot from beyond the arc with just seconds left on the clock turned the tables. This was not the kind of defensive performance the Spurs wanted to showcase, especially considering they had managed to limit the Trail Blazers' scoring opportunities for so long. The 23-second stretch of good defense that preceded Avdija's shot was a rare instance of the team's usually solid defense being breached in such a dramatic fashion. Spurs guard Stephon Castle acknowledged the disappointment of watching that crucial three-pointer drop, saying "It's the NBA, It's the most talented players in the world." We can play 23 seconds of great defense, but they get off a contested 3 and it still gets to drop. The Spurs' offense was unable to overcome a strong showing from the Portland duo of Damian Lillard and Avdija, who combined for impressive performances throughout the game. Lillard's impact was felt immediately as he scored 16 points in the first quarter alone, setting the tone for his team's overall performance. His ability to score effectively early on put pressure on the Spurs' defense from the outset. Avdija made several key contributions down the stretch, including a crucial shot that sealed the win for Portland and sent the Spurs reeling. Despite Castle's efforts to rally his team, Avdija's big shots proved to be too much to overcome. The loss dropped the Spurs to 15-4 on the season, while Portland improved to 12-6 with the victory. The Spurs' loss to Portland has left them tied with three other teams in West Group C pool play, each holding a 2-1 record after three games. A win for San Antonio against Dallas on Friday would secure their spot in the knockout stage, thanks to their significant point differential advantage that will be used as a tiebreaker if needed. Meanwhile, Portland's victory has improved their chances of advancing beyond group stage play, and they can even clinch a wild-card berth with another win over Golden State on Friday. Coach Micah Nori acknowledged his team was given a vote of no confidence in their defensive abilities after he opted to assign 7-foot-2 center to guard Stephon Castle instead of Wembanyama in their previous meeting against the Spurs. The Spurs' high-flying center continued to wreak havoc on opposing defenses, this time in Portland where he found success against the Blazers' big man despite a change in matchups. Wembanyama's ability to adapt and make adjustments on the fly was on full display as he exploited the midrange jumper, a shot that has become a staple of his game. Coach Nori's decision to switch up the lineup seemed to have some effect, but Wembanyama remained a force to be reckoned with, making it clear that he is not easily contained. The Blazers' adjustment helped keep the rest of the Spurs' supporting cast in check, but ultimately proved insufficient against Wembanyama's dominant performance. Wembanyama reflected on his shooting selection after the game, noting that he has been working to improve his shot-making skills and it seems to be paying off. The Spurs' struggles on the road continued, with Vassell's shooting woes a significant contributor to their defeat. His two-game road trip average of 12 shots made from 31 attempts is a concerning trend for the team. Vassell had been out for two games earlier this month due to a groin issue but has since returned to action. However, in the seven games he's played since his return, his field goal percentage has been underwhelming, with only 30 successful shots out of 77 attempts. The Spurs' inability to score consistently is taking its toll on their overall performance, particularly when key players like Dylan Harper and De'Aaron Fox are unavailable. The game had been a thrilling spectacle, with both teams trading blows and neither able to gain a clear advantage. articles.title: Celebrating Thanksgiving in Scotland after nearly two decades abroad
articles.summary: The author, a former study abroad student, grew to appreciate the simplicity and values of Thanksgiving during their time in the US.
articles.content: I made the bold decision to return to Scotland after nearly two decades living in the US, but one tradition has remained steadfast: celebrating Thanksgiving. It all began when I first arrived in the US in 2001 as a study abroad student, and I was perplexed by this peculiar holiday that seemed so deeply ingrained in American culture. But it wasn't long before I grew to appreciate the simplicity of Thanksgiving - the absence of commercialism or religious obligation was refreshing. The idea of taking time out to express gratitude for what one has resonated with me. Celebrating Thanksgiving in Scotland can feel a bit disorienting, but it serves as a vital connection to my life in the US. I've found that embracing this tradition helps me stay rooted in my past while navigating new surroundings. In my early years living in the US, attending Thanksgiving dinners was more of a social obligation than anything else - but as time passed, I began to genuinely appreciate the holiday's spirit and values. As I settled into my new life in Scotland, I found myself missing the sense of community and tradition that had been a big part of my time in the US. Hosting Thanksgiving dinners for friends who were also without family nearby was one way to combat this feeling. I began experimenting with American recipes, adapting them to suit Scottish tastes by adding local ingredients like leeks in cheese sauce, a dish reminiscent of my childhood. My homemade pumpkin cheesecake quickly became an annual request from friends and acquaintances alike. The decision to host Thanksgiving in Scotland wasn't just about recreating a familiar tradition - it also helped me navigate the challenges of rebuilding my life after nearly two decades abroad. Finding a job, securing a new home, and establishing routines were daunting tasks that seemed less overwhelming with something to look forward to. My partner's suggestion to celebrate Thanksgiving was a timely one, as I was struggling to find festive cheer in the shortening days and colder temperatures. His friend from the US, who was feeling homesick at this time of year, also saw the value in hosting an American holiday in Scotland - especially for his two children, who had only experienced it through movies. With a bit of planning, we were able to create a warm and welcoming atmosphere that felt like a true celebration. It was a small but significant way to connect with our community and mark the passing of time in a meaningful way. It's not always easy to get into the Thanksgiving spirit when it feels like the rest of the world is moving on with its daily routine. The first few years after moving back to Scotland from the US were especially challenging. Shopping for ingredients proved to be a bit of an adventure, as some items just weren't readily available in local stores. A can of pumpkin puree, for instance, was nowhere to be found until I stumbled upon it at a health food store - and even then, it came with a hefty price tag of nearly $5 per can. A timely rescue mission by my American friend yielded a bag of fresh cranberries, which helped salvage the shopping trip. Our teenager, usually engrossed in his Rubik's Cube, even took a break to help peel sprouts - although that respite was short-lived. The kids' school friends weren't celebrating Thanksgiving, so our household felt like an oasis of excitement amidst the ordinary routine. After school, the atmosphere shifted, and everyone seemed to be looking forward to the novelty of the holiday. As we sat down to a traditional dinner with all the classics, taking turns to express gratitude was a slightly awkward experience for some guests - but ultimately, it brought everyone together. The sweet potatoes with marshmallows were a sight to behold for my Scottish friends, their faces reflecting a mix of confusion and curiosity as they observed this quintessential American tradition. Despite the initial bewilderment, it soon became apparent that Thanksgiving is a holiday that can transcend cultural boundaries and adapt to different settings. The key lies in its underlying values: gratitude, sharing, and connection with loved ones. For me, Thanksgiving has become a way to stay connected to my American roots, even after living abroad for nearly two decades. It's a tradition that I've managed to incorporate into my new life in Scotland, making it feel like home. In recent years, we've made an effort to observe Thanksgiving on almost every occasion, often hosting small gatherings with our partner and their daughter. However, last year was special, it coincided with a visit from our Swedish friends, and our tiny apartment became the unlikely venue for a lively celebration. As I rummage through the aisles of Scottish supermarkets in search of essential ingredients, I'm struck by the stark price differences between here and the US. A can of pumpkin puree is now a luxury item that costs more than a gallon of gas back home, a far cry from the abundance we often take for granted in America. After settling back into Scottish life, I discovered ways to adapt Thanksgiving traditions to local ingredients and tastes. For instance, butternut squash or sweet potato puree can substitute for pumpkin in recipes, while red currants or sour cherries offer a cranberry-like flavor. Moving back to Scotland after nearly two decades abroad was not a straightforward process. Leaving behind friends, familiar routines, and the life I had built took some getting used to. However, holding onto Thanksgiving traditions has helped me maintain a connection to my American heritage while building a new life in Scotland. Organizing a mini Turkey Trot before dinner is another way for me to incorporate this tradition into my Scottish home, even if it requires an early morning start. articles.title: Cas12m Protein Family Can Cut DNA After All
articles.summary: A new study has revealed that some members of the Cas12m protein family have an active state capable of cleaving DNA.
articles.content: Researchers at the University of Tokyo have made a groundbreaking discovery about the Cas12m protein family, long considered the "black sheep" of the Cas protein clan due to their inability to cut DNA. Until now, scientists had been puzzled by the fact that these proteins, despite being relatively small and potentially more easily deliverable into cells, were unable to perform the crucial function of cutting DNA. However, a new study has shed light on the structural differences between active and inactive Cas12m variants. The research team, led by graduate student Hayato Morinaga and Assistant Professor Satoshi N. Omura, found that some Cas12m proteins do indeed have an active state capable of cleaving DNA. This breakthrough opens up new possibilities for developing compact genome-editing tools. These tools could potentially revolutionize biomedical research, medicine, and biotechnology by providing a more efficient and targeted way to edit genes. The study's findings were published in the journal Nature Chemical Biology, offering a significant step forward in understanding the complex world of gene editing. The research team behind the study decided to investigate further whether the lack of DNA cutting ability in some Cas12m proteins was a common trait among all members of this group or if there were still active ones waiting to be discovered. To understand which molecular characteristics contributed to the inactivity of these proteins, the researchers developed a screening system using laboratory bacteria that could test multiple Cas12m candidates and identify those capable of cutting DNA. This allowed them to search for active Cas12m proteins among many potential candidates. The team's efforts paid off as they discovered some Cas12m proteins that were indeed able to cut DNA. However, the researchers still needed to determine what distinguished these active proteins from their inactive counterparts. Using cryo-electron microscopy, a technique that can reveal detailed three-dimensional molecular structures at the atomic scale, the researchers obtained images of both active and inactive Cas12m proteins. Researchers had been trying to pinpoint which amino acids were crucial for Cas12m proteins' ability to cut DNA. Their investigation involved modifying specific amino acids and testing how these changes affected the protein's function. This approach ultimately led them to identify key differences between active and inactive Cas12m variants. The discovery marks a significant milestone in understanding the complex mechanisms governing Cas12m nuclease activation, which is crucial for its application in genome editing. With this knowledge, scientists can now focus on optimizing the performance of these proteins, with the ultimate goal of developing them into practical tools for precise genetic manipulation.
